title: Schema Composition and Runtime Models
readerIntent: Understand inheritance, layered merging, model generation, and provider delegation.
owner: Nodics schema, data-model, and database capabilities
summary: Nodics composes schema definitions at runtime, supplies the base contract where appropriate, and creates models that interact through provider-neutral data services.

sections.heading: Composition
items: The owning module declares its schema-specific properties and policies.
Framework base properties are composed at runtime; a schema should not repeat inherited declarations merely to imitate generated output.
A layered project module may refine supported properties without replacing the original authority.
The effective schema is validated before the runtime model becomes available.

sections.heading: Runtime model behavior
items: Resolve tenant and module context.
Load the effective schema and provider configuration.
Apply authorization, validation, interceptors, lifecycle rules, and transaction policy.
Delegate persistence to the configured database model handler.
Trigger configured cache, search, event, audit, or versioning behavior through their owned contracts.

sections.heading: Optional capabilities
paragraphs: Search, caching, versioning, publishing, and workflow are enabled per owning module or schema according to configuration. Their metadata must not imply that every record automatically uses every capability.

sections.heading: Base behavior and inheritance
paragraphs: Nodics supplies common base behavior at runtime where required. A schema declares owned differences and does not repeat super: base merely as boilerplate when composition already supplies it.
Explicit inheritance remains appropriate for a non-default parent or when the parent relationship is itself contractual. Effective-schema evidence makes the result inspectable.

sections.heading: Layered schema extension
items: The reusable capability defines the original schema meaning.
A later project layer may refine supported fields, metadata, validation, permissions, indexes, or relationships.
Conflicting type or ownership changes require migration and compatibility decisions.
Customizable access rules belong in owned properties, not closed constants.
Composition remains deterministic for reviewers and AI tools.

sections.heading: Runtime initialization
items: Configuration selects modules and providers.
Definitions are discovered and composed in load order.
Effective schemas are validated before readiness.
Database services translate schemas and indexes through the configured adapter.
Item and search models become available to services and routes.
Failures prevent false readiness and retain diagnostics.

sections.heading: Item and search models
paragraphs: The item model represents authoritative record operations through provider-neutral persistence. The search model represents normalized discovery. They share owning schema context but serve different responsibilities.
Every model can be searchable without requiring every model to use an external engine. Simple queries may use persistence; advanced indexing uses a configured search provider.

sections.heading: Versioning and publishing
paragraphs: Versioning is enabled through module or schema configuration, not copied fields in every schema. A staged catalog may retain versions and approvals while a separate online system consumes the published representation.
The existing publishing capability owns staged-to-online transfer. Composition contributes versioned shape only when enabled.

sections.heading: Schema evolution
items: Optional additive fields normally carry lower migration risk.
Index changes require provider-qualified rollout.
Rename, removal, type, and ownership changes require migration and compatibility.
Search, cache, import/export, events, generated APIs, and docs evolve together.
Staged and online schemas remain compatible during publishing rollout.

sections.heading: Example and verification
paragraphs: Profile defines Enterprise. A project adds an optional regulatory identifier through a later schema layer while retaining base audit fields, Tenant relationship, ownership, and existing indexes.

Verify effective schemas with and without the project, valid CRUD/search/import/export, conflicting extensions, provider failure, tenant isolation, versioning enabled and disabled, migration, and generated contracts.
